name: Pai Gow
description: Pai Gow is an ancient Chinese gambling game played with a specialized set of thirty-two Chinese domino tiles. Each player is dealt four tiles which they must partition into two separate pairs: a high-ranking hand and a low-ranking hand. The objective is to outrank both of the banker's corresponding pairs, requiring deep knowledge of the complex and non-numeric tile ranking hierarchy.

content.text: Pai Gow is an ancient Chinese gambling game played with a specialized set of thirty-two Chinese domino tiles. Each player is dealt four tiles which they must partition into two separate pairs: a high-ranking hand and a low-ranking hand. The objective is to outrank both of the banker's corresponding pairs, requiring deep knowledge of the complex and non-numeric tile ranking hierarchy.
Pai Gow (牌九) dates back to the Song Dynasty and is the ancestor of many modern partition games including Pai Gow Poker.
Up to eight players sit around a table; the role of banker rotates among players counter-clockwise.
A unique set of thirty-two tiles where eleven specific tiles are duplicated to form matched pairs.
32 Chinese dominoes, a 'Chung' marker for the banker, and three dice to determine the deal order.
Tiles are stacked in a 4x8 woodpile; dice are rolled to select which player receives the first stack.

items.text: Bonanza Pai Gow: Casino variant offering side bets on specific tile combinations and bonuses for high-ranking hands.
Commission Play: The house takes a 5% commission on all winning bets placed by players against the bank.
Player Banking: A rule allowing players to take turns acting as the banker, gaining the advantage of winning copy hands.
